prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 5 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a landscape 16:9 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One storyboard image with five painted panels in shot order, arranged three across and two down; leave the lower-right grid position blank. Use plain gutters and no drawn text, labels, numbers or arrows. Soft early-morning overcast light, fine rain, wet asphalt reflections, muted grey, beige and leaf-green surroundings, natural restrained contrast and consistent 6000K daylight unite every panel. Kasun is a smooth, featureless red artist's mannequin of medium height and lean build; Anudi is a smooth, featureless blue mannequin of average height and slender build. Anudi carries an open navy folding umbrella in her left hand and a structured tan handbag on her right shoulder, with brass-coloured fittings and an open exterior side pocket. The smartphone has an orange back, three large camera circles and a transparent case. Kasun's compact food three-wheeler has muted ochre panels and a dark rain canopy. Render the location and props realistically while keeping both people entirely mannequin-like.

Geography: The route runs west to east, always screen left to screen right. The three-wheeler occupies the western vending bay; immediately east is the walking-edge patch where the phone falls, followed by a short pursuit stretch and then the encounter position several paces farther east. All cameras remain on the pavement side, south of the travel axis, looking outward across the walking strip toward the road, so the mannequins travel across the frame rather than into depth. A slab-covered open kerb drain borders the near side of the walking strip. Across the road, a long weathered concrete boundary wall has a recognisable pale-green section toward the western end; this section remains on frame left as the camera positions progress east. Farther east, bare sections of that same wall, a utility pole and an opening beneath leafy trees progressively enter the backgrounds.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Pavement side of the axis, looking outward across the route; waist-height camera, 35mm wide framing with both full figures, the entire umbrella and clear ground beneath the handbag. Background: The three-wheeler occupies frame left. Across the wet road, the pale-green section of the boundary wall is background left, with weathered bare concrete extending right; the kerb drain crosses the lower foreground. The red mannequin stands upright beside the three-wheeler at frame left, chest and head turned right toward the passing blue mannequin, both empty hands lowered. At frame right, the blue mannequin is caught mid-stride toward screen right, chest and head facing along the route, left hand gripping the open umbrella shaft and right hand holding the orange phone beside the handbag's open pocket. The handbag hangs from its right shoulder, with uninterrupted space visible between the pocket and the wet roadside below.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Pavement side, slightly east of the first setup, looking across the same left-to-right route; waist-height 35mm wide framing showing Anudi's full figure and the ground beneath her bag. Background: The three-wheeler and Kasun are outside the left edge. The pale-green wall section remains at background left, bare concrete occupies the centre and right, and the wet drain slabs run across the lower foreground. The blue mannequin occupies centre-right in a rightward walking stride, chest and head still directed screen right. Its left hand holds the umbrella upright, its handbag remains on the right shoulder, and its now-empty right hand is beside the open exterior pocket. The orange phone is just below the pocket, separated from the hand and suspended above the wet walking edge, with its transparent case and orange back readable.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Pavement side of the established axis, looking across the route; slightly low camera at approximately 90 centimetres, 35mm medium-wide framing retaining Kasun's upright figure and the ground immediately ahead. Background: A cropped portion of the three-wheeler sits at far left, with the pale-green boundary-wall section behind it on background left. Wet asphalt and bare wall extend toward the open right side; drain slabs occupy the near lower edge. The red mannequin stands at frame left with its chest facing right and its head angled down-right toward the orange phone lying at lower centre. Both hands are empty and lowered beside its upright body, with the right hand nearest the phone. The handset rests orange-back-up on the wet walking edge just ahead, and clear roadside space continues toward screen right.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Pavement side, farther east along the route, looking slightly obliquely across it without crossing the axis; standing eye-height, 50mm waist-up medium shot in three-quarter side view. Background: The same pale-green wall section is now a narrow feature at far background left. A longer bare concrete section fills the middle background, with a utility pole and leafy opening toward frame right; the three-wheeler is outside the frame. The red mannequin is left of centre in a forward-leaning rightward running pose, chest facing screen right and head turned toward Anudi's position beyond the right edge. Its right hand holds the orange phone beside its waist, clearly inside the lower frame, while its empty left hand is drawn back with the bent arm. Leave open space ahead on the right and keep the three-quarter head orientation readable against the softened wall.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Pavement side of the same axis, looking outward across the route; standing eye-height, 40mm two-shot from knees upward, including the umbrella canopy and a clear gap between both figures. Background: The pale-green boundary-wall section remains at far background left, with the utility pole now left of centre. Bare concrete and the leafy roadside opening occupy background right, while a narrow strip of wet walking surface appears below the figures. The blue mannequin stands at frame right with chest and head still facing right, left hand holding the open umbrella and empty right hand lowered beside the handbag on its right shoulder. The red mannequin approaches from frame left in a rightward stepping pose, chest and head facing right toward the blue mannequin. Its right hand still holds the phone near its hip rather than extending it, and its empty left hand is loosely bent beside its body, with visible space separating the two mannequins.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
